After consecutive weeks of only having weekly usage caps, OpenAI announced today that it will restore the five-hour usage limit for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work. Details below.

The five-hour usage cap is once again applied to ChatGPT Plus subscribers

OpenAI Codex and ChatGPT Engineering lead Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), Plus users will once again have the five-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work.

Once users exhaust the five-hour or weekly limit, they can wait for the next cycle to reset usage, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI will also occasionally reset usage for users for free, and users can earn reserve resets through designated promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI had temporarily lifted the five-hour usage limit on Codex and ChatGPT Work, retaining only the weekly cap.

During this period, the company also repeatedly reset weekly usage for users ahead of schedule to celebrate reaching multiple milestones, including one million additional active users across the two (now merged) platforms.

However, as Tibo explained tonight on X:

"Tomorrow we will be restoring the 5-hour limit for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex. I had mentioned this earlier and then delayed. Here’s why: (a) the 5-hour limit helps us spread compute evenly, which keeps the weekly allotment for the plan generous; (b) Plus users are mostly lighter or newer users, and they often unwittingly burn through their entire weekly allotment and then feel confused with a worse experience. In the coming months, Pro $100 and Pro $200 subscriptions will continue to have no 5-hour limit."

Tibo did not mention any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently use a separate credit-based usage system.

Will the restoration of the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
